title: A malformed `--seeds` line panics or fails without naming the file or line
body:
`Seeds::from_path` (nail/src/io/seeds.rs) reads a seeds file with one of two functions. `Seeds::new`, used without `--max-seeds`, indexes `tokens[0]` through `tokens[7]` with no check of the column count. `Seeds::new_max` checks the count, but its errors call the file "mmseqs align tsv". Both parse the numeric columns with a bare `parse()?`. The same functions read the file `mmseqs convertalis` writes, so a message has to fit both sources.

The input survey on nail-d551f7 ran these against the release binary, except the last row, which was read from the code:

| Line in the `--seeds` file | What the user sees |
|---|---|
| fewer than 8 columns, no `--max-seeds` | `index out of bounds: the len is 4 but the index is 4` |
| a blank line, a trailing one included | `index out of bounds: the len is 0 but the index is 0` |
| a non-number in columns 3 to 8 | `error: invalid digit found in string` |
| wrong column count, with `--max-seeds` | `unexpected line format in mmseqs align tsv` |
| unsorted file, with `--max-seeds` | `unexpected sorting of mmseqs align tsv` |

## Proposal

Both readers check the column count. Each error names the file, the line number and the column.

## Open

- whether a blank line is skipped or is an error
close_reason: parse_seed in nail/src/io/seeds.rs serves both readers, checks for 8 fields and names the line and field on failure. Blank lines are skipped, per Jack. The file name comes from Seeds::from_path. Committed on dev.
